Godot Introduction.exp: Introduction to Godot and its ecosystem.

Hello Godot:
Godot uses a scene-based architecture. Every game is built with nodes arranged in a tree. The main script extends Node or one of its subclasses like Node2D, Sprite2D, or CharacterBody2D. GDScript is Godot's primary scripting language — it's Python-like and deeply integrated with the engine.

To start, create a scene with a Node2D root, attach a GDScript, and use the _ready() function for initialization. Run your scene to see the output.

extends Node

# Called when the node enters the scene tree for the first time.
func _ready():
    print("Hello, Godot!")
    print("Welcome to game development!")

# Called every frame. 'delta' is the elapsed time since the previous frame.
func _process(delta):
    # Game logic runs here each frame
    pass

TileSet & TileMapLayer: The TileMapLayer node creates grid-based levels. A TileSet resource defines tiles with physics layers, navigation polygons, and terrain definitions for auto-tiling. You can add custom data per tile. Use terrain bits for automatic tile connection (like biome blending). Animated and random tiles add visual variety without code.

extends TileMapLayer

func _ready():
    # Programmatic tileset
    var tileset = TileSet.new()
    var source = TileSetAtlasSource.new()
    source.texture = preload("res://assets/tileset.png")
    source.texture_region_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
    
    # Add alternative tiles (for random variation)
    source.create_alternative_tile(Vector2i(1, 0))
    source.create_alternative_tile(Vector2i(2, 0))
    tileset.add_source(source)
    
    # Set tile
    set_cell(Vector2i(5, 3), 0, Vector2i(0, 0))
    
    # Terrain auto-tiling
    # Configure terrain sets in TileSet editor,
    # then use:
    set_cells_terrain_connect(get_used_cells(), 0, 0)
    
    # Navigation layer on tiles
    tileset.set_navigation_layer(0)
    
    # Physics layer on tiles
    tileset.set_physics_layer(0)
    
    # Custom data
    tileset.set_custom_data("damage", Variant.Type.TYPE_INT)
    var data = get_cell_tile_data(Vector2i(5, 3))
    if data:
        var damage = data.get_custom_data("damage")

Scene Tree: Every Godot game is a tree of nodes. A scene is a collection of nodes organized hierarchically. Nodes can be added, removed, and rearranged at runtime. The SceneTree manages all active nodes and handles processing, rendering, and input.

Types & Syntax: GDScript is dynamically typed with optional static typing. Use : Type to declare types. The @export annotation exposes variables in the inspector. @onready defers initialization until the node is ready. Match statements provide powerful pattern matching. Lambda functions with func syntax are first-class citizens.

extends CharacterBody2D

@export var speed: float = 300.0
@export var jump_velocity: float = -400.0
@onready var sprite: Sprite2D = $Sprite2D

func _ready() -> void:
    var items = ["sword", "potion", "shield"]
    for item in items:
        match item:
            "sword":
                print("Equipping sword!")
            "potion":
                print("Drinking potion!")
            _:
                print("Unknown item: ", item)
    
    # Lambda
    var double = func(x: int) -> int: return x * 2
    print(double(5))
    
    # Type inference
    var health := 100
    var name := "Hero"

PhysicsBody & Collisions: Godot provides three physics body types: StaticBody (non-moving obstacles), RigidBody (full physics simulation), and CharacterBody (kinematic movement with custom logic). Use move_and_slide() for CharacterBody movement with automatic collision resolution. Collision layers and masks control which objects interact.

Event System: Signals are Godot's built-in event system. They are type-safe and can be connected in the editor or via code. Custom signals are declared with the signal keyword. Groups tag nodes for bulk operations — call methods on all group members or get all nodes in a group. Use CONNECT_ONE_SHOT for one-time connections and CONNECT_DEFERRED for safe cross-frame calls.

extends Node

signal health_changed(old_value: int, new_value: int)
signal died()
signal item_collected(item: String, count: int)

@export var health := 100

func take_damage(amount: int) -> void:
    var old = health
    health -= amount
    if health <= 0:
        health = 0
        died.emit()
    health_changed.emit(old, health)

func _ready():
    # Connect with flags
    health_changed.connect(_on_health_changed, CONNECT_ONE_SHOT)
    
    # Groups
    add_to_group("enemies")
    add_to_group("attackable")
    
    # Call on all group members
    get_tree().call_group("enemies", "pause")
    
    # Get all nodes in group
    var enemies = get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")
    
    # Check if in group
    if is_in_group("players"):
        print("Is a player!")

CanvasItem & Spatial: Godot supports three shader types: canvas_item (2D nodes), spatial (3D nodes), and particles (particle systems). Shaders use a GLSL-like language with Godot-specific uniforms and built-ins. VisualShader provides a node-based editor for creating shaders without code. Use uniforms to expose parameters to the inspector.

Input Map & Actions: Godot's Input Map in Project Settings defines named actions bound to keys, buttons, or controller axes. Use Input.get_action_strength() for analog input (trigger pressure, joystick). The _input(event) callback processes individual events, while _process() or _physics_process() polling handles continuous input. Action names enable easy rebinding.

AnimationPlayer & AnimationTree: The AnimationPlayer node animates any node property via keyframes. AnimationTree adds state machine blending with parameters. Blend spaces (1D/2D) blend between animations based on a parameter like speed or direction. Root motion allows animations to drive character movement. Use AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback to control state transitions.

Audio & Buses: Godot uses an audio bus system for routing and effects. AudioStreamPlayer plays 2D sounds, AudioStreamPlayer2D/3D provides positional audio. The Audio bus layout allows adding effects like reverb, EQ, compression, and distortion per bus. Use AudioServer for global control. Stream players support OGG, MP3, and WAV formats.

Resource System: Resources are reusable data containers saved as .tres (text) or .res (binary). They store game data like item definitions, stats, dialogue trees, and level configs. Create custom resources by extending the Resource class. Resources are cached by default — use preload() or load() to access them. Use .duplicate() for unique runtime instances.

@tool & EditorPlugin: Scripts with the @tool annotation run in the editor, enabling live preview and custom tools. Use EditorPlugin to add docks, buttons, menu items, and inspector plugins. Create custom gizmos for in-editor manipulation. Build importers, exporters, and level editors that extend Godot's functionality without modifying the engine itself.

tool
extends EditorPlugin

const MainDock = preload("res://addons/my_tool/dock.tscn")
var dock_instance: Control

func _enter_tree() -> void:
    # Add toolbar button
    add_tool_menu_item("Generate Level", Callable(self, "_generate_level"))
    
    # Add dock to editor
    dock_instance = MainDock.instantiate()
    add_control_to_dock(DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_UR, dock_instance)
    
    # Custom inspector plugin for ItemData
    var inspector_plugin = preload("res://addons/my_tool/item_inspector_plugin.gd").new()
    add_inspector_plugin(inspector_plugin)

func _exit_tree() -> void:
    remove_tool_menu_item("Generate Level")
    remove_control_from_docks(dock_instance)
    dock_instance.queue_free()

func _generate_level() -> void:
    # @tool allows editor-level operations
    var root = Node3D.new()
    root.name = "GeneratedLevel"
    get_editor_interface().get_edited_scene_root().add_child(root)
    root.owner = get_editor_interface().get_edited_scene_root()

C++ Bindings: GDExtension (Godot 4) allows writing C++ libraries that dynamically link without recompiling the engine. Ideal for performance-critical systems like custom physics, pathfinding, or audio processing. Classes registered via GDExtension are fully accessible from GDScript. Replaces the GDNative system from Godot 3. Uses the godot-cpp bindings library for C++ API access.

OpenXR + Render Modes: Godot 4 offers three renderers: forward_plus (desktop, many lights, SSAO, glow), mobile (faster, simpler, for mobile), and gl_compatibility (OpenGL fallback). XR support via OpenXR — use XROrigin3D, XRCamera3D, and XRController3D. Supports hand tracking, passthrough AR, and standalone headsets.

Sprites, Layers & Effects: Sprite2D displays textures with properties like centered, flip, offset, and modulate. AnimatedSprite2D plays sprite sheet animations via the SpriteFrames resource. CanvasLayer separates rendering layers for parallax or UI. Viewport renders to a texture for mini-maps, security cameras, or in-game screens. Light2D adds 2D dynamic lighting with shadow caster occlusion.

extends Node2D

@onready var sprite := $Sprite2D as Sprite2D
@onready var anim_sprite := $AnimatedSprite2D as AnimatedSprite2D

func _ready() -> void:
    # Sprite2D properties
    sprite.texture = preload("res://assets/character.png")
    sprite.centered = true
    sprite.flip_h = false
    sprite.offset = Vector2(0, -8)
    sprite.modulate = Color(1, 0.5, 0.5, 1)  # tint red
    
    # AnimatedSprite2D
    anim_sprite.sprite_frames = preload("res://assets/run_frames.tres")
    anim_sprite.play("run")
    anim_sprite.animation_finished.connect(_on_anim_finished)
    
    # CanvasLayer for parallax
    var layer = CanvasLayer.new()
    layer.layer = -1  # behind everything
    add_child(layer)
    
    # Viewport for mini-map
    var viewport = SubViewport.new()
    viewport.size = Vector2i(256, 256)
    viewport.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS
    var mini_map = Sprite2D.new()
    mini_map.texture = viewport.get_texture()
    add_child(mini_map)
    
    # 2D Light
    # $Light2D.enabled = true
    # $Light2D.shadow_color = Color.BLACK
    # $Light2D.energy = 1.5

3D Nodes & Environment: Godot 4 uses Node3D as the base for all 3D nodes. MeshInstance3D renders meshes with materials. Lighting includes DirectionalLight3D (sun), OmniLight3D (point), and SpotLight3D (cone). WorldEnvironment controls sky, ambient light, fog, and tonemapping. VoxelGI and SDFGI provide real-time global illumination.

extends Node3D

@onready var mesh := $MeshInstance3D as MeshInstance3D
@onready var light := $DirectionalLight3D as DirectionalLight3D
@onready var env := $WorldEnvironment as WorldEnvironment

func _ready() -> void:
    # Mesh and material
    var box = BoxMesh.new()
    box.size = Vector3(2, 2, 2)
    var material = StandardMaterial3D.new()
    material.albedo_color = Color(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)
    material.metallic = 0.3
    material.roughness = 0.4
    mesh.mesh = box
    mesh.material_override = material
    
    # Directional light (sun)
    light.light_energy = 1.0
    light.light_indirect_energy = 0.5
    light.shadow_enabled = true
    light.light_bake_mode = Light3D.BAKE_SDFGI
    
    # WorldEnvironment
    env.environment.background_mode = Environment.BG_SKY
    var sky = ProceduralSkyMaterial.new()
    sky.sky_top_color = Color(0.2, 0.5, 1.0)
    sky.sky_horizon_color = Color(0.8, 0.8, 0.8)
    env.environment.sky = Sky.new()
    env.environment.sky.sky_material = sky
    env.environment.ssao_enabled = true
    env.environment.ssao_radius = 2.0
    env.environment.glow_enabled = true
    
    # VoxelGI for baked GI
    # var gi = VoxelGI.new()
    # gi.extend = Vector3(20, 10, 20)
    # add_child(gi)
    # gi.bake()

Control Nodes & Theming: Godot's UI system uses Control nodes: Button, Label, TextureRect, Panel, Container (HBox, VBox, Grid, Margin). Theme resources define colors, fonts, icons, and styles across all UI elements. Use Theme.duplicate() for runtime theme variants. StyleBoxFlat, StyleBoxTexture, and StyleBoxLine style individual elements.

Procedural Content: Godot's FastNoiseLite provides Perlin, Simplex, Cellular, and Value noise for procedural generation. Use NoiseTexture2D to generate texture-based noise. SurfaceTool builds custom meshes programmatically. Combine with ArrayMesh for complex procedural geometry. Generate terrain heightmaps, cave systems, and infinite worlds using chunk-based loading.

extends Node3D

func _ready() -> void:
    # FastNoiseLite setup
    var noise = FastNoiseLite.new()
    noise.noise_type = FastNoiseLite.TYPE_PERLIN
    noise.fractal_type = FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_FBM
    noise.fractal_octaves = 6
    noise.fractal_lacunarity = 2.0
    noise.fractal_gain = 0.5
    noise.frequency = 0.05
    noise.seed = randi()
    
    # Sample noise
    var height = noise.get_noise_2d(x, y)
    
    # NoiseTexture2D
    var noise_tex = NoiseTexture2D.new()
    noise_tex.noise = noise
    noise_tex.width = 512
    noise_tex.height = 512
    noise_tex.seamless = true
    
    # Generate terrain mesh
    var st = SurfaceTool.new()
    st.begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES)
    
    var resolution := 64
    var size := 50.0
    for z in range(resolution):
        for x in range(resolution):
            var u = float(x) / (resolution - 1)
            var v = float(z) / (resolution - 1)
            var world_x = (u - 0.5) * size
            var world_z = (v - 0.5) * size
            var h = noise.get_noise_2d(world_x, world_z) * 5.0
            var vertex = Vector3(world_x, h, world_z)
            st.set_uv(Vector2(u, v))
            st.add_vertex(vertex)
    
    # Generate indices
    st.generate_normals()
    var mesh = st.commit()
    
    var mi = MeshInstance3D.new()
    mi.mesh = mesh
    add_child(mi)
    
    # Infinite world: use chunks
    # var chunk = load_chunk(chunk_x, chunk_z)
    # if chunk_position not in loaded_chunks:

File I/O & Save Games: Godot provides FileAccess for binary and text file operations. ConfigFile manages INI-style configs with sections and keys. ResourceSaver and ResourceLoader persist/.res and .tres resources. Use OS.get_user_data_dir() for cross-platform save paths. ZIPPacker/ZIPReader handle compressed archives.

Godot Data.exp: Working with data and APIs in Godot.

Multiplayer API: Godot's high-level multiplayer system syncs game state across the network. MultiplayerSpawner auto-spawns scenes on all peers. MultiplayerSynchronizer replicates properties. Use the @rpc annotation for remote procedure calls with modes: authority, any_peer, call_local, reliable, unreliable. ENetMultiplayerPeer handles low-level connection.

Profiling & Optimization: Godot's Debugger has a Profiler tab (Script, Visual, Servers) and a Monitors tab (FPS, physics time, draw calls). Use Engine.get_frames_per_second() for runtime FPS. Key optimizations: sprite atlasing, MultiMesh instancing, object pooling, disabling off-screen nodes with VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D, and reducing draw calls via batching. Use Performance singleton for custom metrics.

extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
    # Check performance from code
    print("FPS: ", Engine.get_frames_per_second())
    print("Draw calls: ", Performance.get_monitor(Performance.RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME))
    print("Objects: ", Performance.get_monitor(Performance.OBJECT_NODE_COUNT))

func optimize_particles() -> void:
    # Use GPUParticles instead of CPUParticles for many particles
    $GPUParticles2D.amount = 500
    $GPUParticles2D.local_coords = false

func object_pool_example() -> void:
    # Pre-create and reuse
    var pool = []
    for i in range(50):
        var bullet = preload("res://bullet.tscn").instantiate()
        bullet.visible = false
        add_child(bullet)
        pool.append(bullet)
    
    var b = pool.pop_front()
    b.global_position = $Muzzle.global_position
    b.visible = true
    pool.append(b)

func _process(delta: float) -> void:

    var start = Time.get_ticks_usec()
    # ... heavy logic ...
    var elapsed = Time.get_ticks_usec() - start

Export Templates & Platforms: Godot exports to Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS, and Web. Configure export presets in Project > Export. Install export templates via Editor > Manage Export Templates. Set application name, version, icon, and orientation per platform. Use OS.get_name() for platform detection. For mobile: configure AAB/APK signing, permissions, and screen sizes.

extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
    detect_platform()

func detect_platform() -> void:
    match OS.get_name():
        "Windows":
            DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN)
        "Android", "iOS":
            Input.set_screen_orientation(Input.SCREEN_LANDSCAPE)
            DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN)
        "Web":
            JavaScriptBridge.eval("console.log('Game loaded in browser!')")
        "Linux", "macOS":
            DisplayServer.window_set_size(Vector2i(1280, 720))

func setup_export() -> void:
    # Project settings per platform
    ProjectSettings.set_setting("application/config/name", "My Game")
    ProjectSettings.set_setting("application/config/version", "1.0.0")
    ProjectSettings.set_setting("application/config/icon", "res://icon.png")
    
    # Export template paths
    # Windows: ~/.local/share/godot/export_templates/<version>/windows_x86_64_release.exe
    # Android: ~/.local/share/godot/export_templates/<version>/android_release.apk
    
    # For Steam Deck verification
    # ProjectSettings.set_setting("display/window/size/mode", 0)  # Windowed scaling

func get_save_path() -> String:
    # Cross-platform save location
    return ProjectSettings.globalize_path("user://")
